# ops_vcs_connection (Resource)

A VCS connection: an access token for GitHub or Azure DevOps, for registry modules, the template catalog and workspaces linked to a branch. The token is write-only: Terraform can't see a token replaced in the UI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ops_vcs_connection" "ado" {
  name          = "azure-devops"
  provider_type = "azure-devops"
  base_url      = "https://dev.azure.com/my-org"
  token         = var.ado_token
  scope         = "selected"
  project_ids   = [ops_project.prd.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)
- `provider_type` (String) `github` or `azure-devops`.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The access token, checked when set (the provider lists repositories with it). Read access for modules and workspaces; write access for a template catalog the builder saves to.

### Optional

- `base_url` (String) The API URL: for Azure DevOps the organization (`https://dev.azure.com/<org>`); GitHub's by default.
- `project_ids` (Set of String) With scope `selected`: every workspace of these projects may link it.
- `scope` (String) Which workspaces may link its repositories: `""` none, `all`, or `selected` (`project_ids`, `workspace_ids`).
- `workspace_ids` (Set of String) With scope `selected`: these workspaces may link it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# by name or id; set the token in the configuration: OPS doesn't return it
terraform import ops_vcs_connection.ado azure-devops
```
